voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text: Because we are not one person speaking. We are a people speaking of ourselves. That is who we are -- the ones who stood together, who walked the road together, who came back together when we fell. When Rome ordered the sacrifice, some among us paid for the paper and never stood at the altar at all. Cyprian still named them fallen, because holding that paper was a denial. Their hands were clean, but their conscience was not. What made them fallen was not what one pair of hands did alone. It was what the whole body bore together. Augustine taught the same bond in different words. What you do, God does in you. That is not one man's private standing before God. It is the shape of a life held inside something larger than itself. We say we because that is what we are -- a flock held together under one shepherd, not a collection of separate souls who happen to stand in the same room.

names.name: Thascius Caecilius Cyprianus, bishop of Carthage (248/249-258)

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop, chosen while still new to the faith, over his own reluctance. During a plague he taught us to love even our enemies. He was put to death under Valerian.

dates.display: a trained rhetorician who turned from a public career to Christian life, converted c. 246; ordained and elected bishop of Carthage between roughly July 248 and April 249 by the acclamation of the Carthaginian people, over the recorded opposition of five presbyters, while still newly baptised (Doc_01 SS2; lpc.story.election-of-cyprian); banished to Curubis under the Valerianic persecution; executed under the emperor Valerian in 258 (lpc.story.the-death-of-cyprian)

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV, independently re-located this session; Doc_01 SS2); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII; Doc_01 SS2); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo (lpc.story.the-psalms-on-the-wall)

confidence.divergence_note: Cyprian uses the word himself, in De Lapsis and in his letter to Antonianus. The English translation renders libelli as certificates, so the Latin headword is absent from the vendored English volume apart from one occurrence in the Introductory Notice to the anonymous treatise against Novatian. The Latin witnesses carry it. Latin libellus in Cyprian also names the martyrs' petitions, so the split between this term and lpc.term.certificates-letters-of-peace separates the English word and is not a distinction the Latin makes.
